name: Horon
note: Gathered and written by a machine from public sources and checked against them. Not reviewed by a person, not rights-cleared, not tested on learners. The rules are in manifest.json.

card.name: Horon
card.profile: Group folk dances of Turkey’s Eastern Black Sea region in circle/line formation with rapid footwork, jumps and shoulder shimmies; from Greek choros, Pontic Greek roots, 50+ regional variants, typically to kemençe or tulum. NOT UNESCO — the 2021 inscription claim is false.

observation.setting: indoor stage with wooden flooring, Turkish flags in the background, judges seated at tables in the foreground
observation.dancers: mixed group of young men and women in traditional costumes, approximately 20-30 dancers
observation.formation_and_space: starts in two lines entering from sides, forms circles, lines, diagonals, and a straight line across the back; travels around the stage
observation.posture: upright torso, slight knee bounce, weight shifted between feet
observation.footwork: quick stepping, hopping, stamping on the beat, high knee lifts and kicks in sync
observation.arms_and_hands: arms linked or held in W-position or V-position, elbows bent, hands clasped with neighbors
observation.hips_and_torso: minimal hip movement, torso remains upright with gentle vertical bouncing
observation.partnering: group folk dance formation with hand-to-hand holds among dancers, no individual couple partnering
observation.levels_jumps_turns: frequent small hops, jumping with knees raised, spinning in lines or circles
observation.costume_and_props: women wear orange-brown skirts with striped trim and vests over white blouses; men wear dark trousers, white shirts, and black vests
observation.cannot_infer: exact foot weight transitions obscured by long shot camera angles and quick changes

signature_moments.what: dancers enter from the sides in lines performing brisk stepping and hopping moves
dancers form a circle and travel rapidly with synchronized foot stamps
dancers raise arms high in linked V-shape while stepping in a line
close-up of male dancers performing high knee lifts with precise footwork
